Reproducing Tingley and Buzsaki (2019) from dandiset 000218¶

Paper: Tingley D, Buzsaki G (2019). Routing of hippocampal ripples to subcortical structures via the lateral septum. Neuron 105, 138-149. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2019.10.012. The full text was used: the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC6952543). Its supplementary figures were not available, so claims on Figures S1 to S5 rest on the main text.

Dandiset: DANDI:000218 version 0.250624.0439, 98 NWB files (1.5 TB) from 6 rats, streamed from the archive. The paper cites no version (it says the data would go to CRCNS). There are two published versions, 0.220131.1608 and 0.250624.0439; they hold the same 98 files with the same blob ids (checked below) and differ only in contributor metadata, so the most recent one is pinned.

The files hold the LFP at 1250 Hz on every channel, sorted units with a region label in most files, sleep states, epochs and trials. They hold no detected events. LS high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) and CA1 ripples are detected here from the LFP, following the Methods and the buzcode detector they name (see ls_hfo.py). The paper's own code repository holds no analysis of this paper apart from the network model of Figure 8.

Claim Tested here
dataset-composition: 6 rats, 1989 LS neurons, 37 CA1+LS and 25 CA3+LS recordings tested
fig1c-hfo-each-animal: HFOs with increased LS firing in each of 6 animals tested
fig1c-event-count: 29,955 HFOs tested
figs1-participation: 16% of LS neurons per HFO, 0.23 spikes per event tested
fig1d-phase-locking: 92% of LS neurons phase-locked, trough preference tested
fig1f-shorter-than-ripples: LS HFOs 27 ms against CA1 ripples 31 ms tested
fig1g-slower-than-ripples: 147 against 159 Hz tested
fig1h-no-amplitude-frequency-correlation tested
fig2-confined-to-ls: HFOs only at LS sites tested
fig2ef-intermediate-ls: power and locking peak in intermediate LS blocked (metadata insufficient)
fig3-travelling-waves: propagation speeds blocked (metadata insufficient)
fig4b-pre-post-unchanged: excess correlation PRE = POST tested
fig4b-hfo-above-behav: HFO excess correlation above BEHAV and jitter tested
fig4-sessions-few-change: 7 of 53 sessions differ blocked after selection (too few recordings)
fig4c-temporal-bias: PRE and POST biases similar blocked after selection (too few recordings)
fig4d-compression: above chance up to 20-fold tested
figs2-post-rate-increase: rates rise in post-behavior NREM tested
fig5b-nrem-and-rates: HFOs mostly in NREM, rarer than ripples tested
fig5d-lag: CA1 leads LS by 6.4 ms tested
fig5e-state-coupling: coupling 0.3 in NREM against 0.15 in WAKE tested
fig5f-ripple-triggered-firing: higher in NREM tested
fig5f-no-phase-coherence: CA1-LS coherence at chance tested
fig6-optogenetic-hfos blocked (data missing)
fig7e-ca1-spikes: 38% of LS neurons tested
fig7e-state: 26% tested
fig7e-duration: about 20% tested
fig7e-ca1-depth: 23% blocked (data missing)
fig7e-replay: 7.9, 6.6 and 7.1% blocked (methods underspecified)
fig7e-seqnmf: 8.1% blocked (methods underspecified)
fig7e-content-independent blocked (depends on blocked claims)
fig8-model blocked (other: a simulation, no recorded data)

The criteria are in claims/000218/10.1016-j.neuron.2019.10.012.yaml; the outcomes and the reasons are in attempts/000218-tingley-2019-01.yaml.

import collections
import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import requests
from scipy import stats

import ls_hfo

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)

In [2]:
# Stream every file of the pinned version once and keep what the analyses need (about 17 min
# with 6 workers; most of it is loading each file's chunk index over the network).
started = time.time()
asset_list = sorted(ls_hfo.assets(), key=lambda a: a["path"])
results = ls_hfo.run_all([a["path"] for a in asset_list], workers=6)
print(f"dandiset {ls_hfo.DANDISET} version {ls_hfo.VERSION}: {len(asset_list)} files, "
      f"{sum(a['size'] for a in asset_list) / 1e12:.2f} TB")
print(f"streamed and processed in {(time.time() - started) / 60:.1f} min")
errors = [r for r in results if "error" in r]
print("files that failed:", len(errors))
for r in errors:
    print("  ", r["path"], r["error"])
skipped = [r for r in results if "skipped" in r]
print("files without LS electrodes (no LFP analysis):", len(skipped))
for r in skipped:
    print("  ", r["path"], dict(collections.Counter(r["meta"]["el_location"])))
R = [r for r in results if "error" not in r and "skipped" not in r]

# The two published versions hold the same files: compare paths and blob ids.
older = {a["path"]: a["blob"] for a in ls_hfo.assets("0.220131.1608")}
pinned = {a["path"]: a["blob"] for a in asset_list}
print("0.220131.1608 and the pinned version hold the same paths and blobs:", older == pinned)

# Inventory: what each file holds.
def region_counts(values):
    return dict(sorted(collections.Counter(values).items()))

inv = []
for r in results:
    m = r["meta"]
    loc = m["units"]["location"]
    inv.append({
        "file": r["path"].split("/")[1].replace("_ecephys.nwb", "").replace("_behavior+ecephys.nwb", "")[:48],
        "subject": m["subject"], "hours": round(m["duration"] / 3600, 2),
        "electrodes": region_counts(m["el_location"]),
        "units": len(m["units"]["spikes"]),
        "unit_regions": "no location column" if loc is None else region_counts(loc),
        "states": m["states"] is not None, "epochs": m["epochs"] is not None,
        "trials": 0 if m["trials"] is None else len(m["trials"]["start"]),
    })
inv = pd.DataFrame(inv)
print(inv.to_string())
print()
print("files per subject:", inv.subject.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
unit_regions = collections.Counter()
for r in results:
    loc = r["meta"]["units"]["location"]
    if loc is None:
        unit_regions["(no location)"] += len(r["meta"]["units"]["spikes"])
    else:
        unit_regions.update(loc)
print("units by region label:", dict(unit_regions))
print("files whose units have no location column:",
      [r["path"].split("/")[1][:40] for r in results if r["meta"]["units"]["location"] is None and len(r["meta"]["units"]["spikes"])])
print("LFP rates (Hz):", sorted({r["meta"]["lfp_rate"] for r in results}),
      "| conversion:", sorted({r["meta"]["lfp_conversion"] for r in results}), sorted({r["meta"]["lfp_unit"] for r in results}))
print("electrode x, y, z all NaN in every file:", all(np.isnan(r["meta"]["el_xyz"]).all() for r in results))

print("LFP starting_time values (s):", sorted({r["meta"]["lfp_starting_time"] for r in results}))
print("units-table columns:", sorted({tuple(r["meta"]["units"]["columns"]) for r in results}))
print("first unit of the first file with a group_id column, by animal:")
for subj in sorted({r["meta"]["subject"] for r in results}):
    r = next(r for r in results if r["meta"]["subject"] == subj and "group_id" in r["meta"]["units"]["first_row"])
    print("  ", subj, r["meta"]["units"]["first_row"])
unit_groups_ok = all(set(r["meta"]["units"]["group"]) <= set(r["meta"]["el_group"]) for r in results if r["meta"]["units"]["group"] is not None)
print("every unit group_id is an electrode group of its file:", unit_groups_ok)
print("electrode group descriptions:", sorted({g["description"].split()[-1] for r in results for g in r["meta"]["electrode_groups"].values()}),
      "| e.g.", sorted({g["description"] for r in results for g in r["meta"]["electrode_groups"].values()})[:2])
print("devices (name: description), over all files:")
for name, desc in sorted({(k, v) for r in results for k, v in r["meta"]["devices"].items()}):
    print("  ", name, ":", desc)

The archive's summary gives 6 subjects, which matches the 6 rats (DT1, DT2, DT5, DT7, DT8, DT9) and the paper's 5 rats of Tingley and Buzsaki (2018) plus one tetrode rat. DT1 holds LS channels only, without sleep states, epochs or trials, which fits the tetrode rat used only in the phase-locking analysis; the files do not say which rat is which.

Unit region labels: ls, hpc, ca3, and a few cortical, septal and fimbria labels. The hpc label does not separate CA1 from other hippocampal sites. Nine files have units without a location column; their 268 units cannot be assigned to a region and are left out of every unit analysis. The LFP is stored at 1250 Hz as int16 with a conversion of 1.95e-7 V (0.195 uV) per step. The electrode x, y and z are NaN in every file, so the probe geometry and its orientation in the brain are not in the files. Where the units table has a location column it holds clu_id, group_id and location besides the spike times; the nine files without it hold only the ids and spike times. No file has unit waveforms, a peak channel or a quality metric. group_id names an electrode group, and each group is one shank of a probe (the electrode groups are described only as "GroupN electrodes."), so it is used as the shank. The device names give the probe layouts (shanks by sites per shank), without site pitch or the orientation of the probe in the brain. One device, "Neuronexus probe (4 x 1)", is described as "reference sites a few millimeters dorsal" to the rest. The LFP starts at 0 s in every file, the same origin as the spikes, states and trials.

No recording is deposited twice: no two files share an LFP length, the checksum of the first 10 s of their LS channel, or the spike counts of all their units.

25 units in 10 files have spike times out of order (1 to 2782 inversions each), a break of the NWB rule that spike times are sorted. Spike times are sorted here before use. One ppc unit in DT8 ends 6.7 s before the recording; all spikes fall inside the recordings.

Sleep states cover 82 to 100% of each recording that has them, with the labels Non-REM, Awake, MA (microarousal) and REM. Epochs are named before trials, during trials and after trials, and in every file the middle epoch runs from the first trial's start to the last trial's stop, so the epochs are derived from the trials table. They are used as PRE, BEHAV and POST.

Detection counts are summed by animal for each step of the detector: threshold crossings, after merging, after the 5 SD peak test, after the duration limits, and after the EMG check. The EMG check removes 19,684 LS events (23% of those that pass the other steps). LS HFO counts differ widely between animals; DT7 contributes more than half of them (38,008 of 67,186). Only 5 channels in 3 files were dropped as bad.

Unit firing rates are low (median 0.18 to 0.63 Hz for the hpc, ca3 and ls units). 11 units fire above 50 Hz on average; the files carry no isolation quality or single-unit label, so all units are kept.

# Do the spikes, LFP, sleep states and trials share one clock?
# (1) Spikes against LFP: locking of spikes to the 120-200 Hz phase with the spikes shifted in time.
for key, name in (("clock_hpc", "hippocampal units, inside CA1 ripples"), ("clock_ls", "LS units, inside high-power epochs")):
    curves = [r[key] for r in R if r.get(key) is not None and np.isfinite(r[key]["r"]).all()]
    shifts = np.array(curves[0]["shifts_ms"])
    M = np.array([c["r"] for c in curves])
    best = shifts[M.argmax(axis=1)]
    print(f"{name}: {len(curves)} recordings; median resultant by shift (ms):",
          dict(zip(shifts.tolist(), np.round(np.median(M, axis=0), 3).tolist())))
    print(f"   recordings whose locking peaks within +-2 ms of zero shift: {np.sum(np.abs(best) <= 2)} of {len(best)};"
          f" peaks elsewhere: {sorted(collections.Counter(best[np.abs(best) > 2].tolist()).items())}")
    names = [r["path"].split("/")[1][:34] for r in R if r.get(key) is not None and np.isfinite(r[key]["r"]).all()]
    print("   off zero:", [(n, int(b)) for n, b in zip(names, best) if abs(b) > 2])

# (2) Sleep states against LFP: CA1 ripples should fall in NREM far more than in WAKE.
def rate_in(times, states, label, shift=0.0):
    sel = states["label"] == label
    s0, s1 = states["start"][sel] + shift, states["stop"][sel] + shift
    order = np.argsort(s0)
    n = ls_hfo.counts_in(np.sort(times), s0[order], s1[order]).sum()
    return n / (s1 - s0).sum()

rows = []
for r in R:
    if "hpc_events" in r and r["meta"]["states"] is not None:
        st, t = r["meta"]["states"], r["hpc_events"]["peak"]
        row = {"file": r["path"].split("/")[1][:30]}
        for sh in (-600, 0, 600):
            row[sh] = rate_in(t, st, "Non-REM", sh) / max(rate_in(t, st, "Awake", sh), 1e-9)
        rows.append(row)
cl = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"\nCA1 ripple rate in NREM / WAKE over {len(cl)} recordings, median: true labels {cl[0].median():.2f}, "
      f"labels shifted -10 min {cl[-600].median():.2f}, +10 min {cl[600].median():.2f}; "
      f"true labels give the largest ratio in {(cl[0] >= cl[[-600, 600]].max(axis=1)).sum()} of {len(cl)}")

# (3) Trials against states: the animal is awake on the maze, so trial time should not be scored NREM.
rows = []
for r in R:
    m = r["meta"]
    if m["states"] is not None and m["trials"] is not None:
        st = m["states"]
        nrem = st["label"] == "Non-REM"
        row = {}
        for sh in (-3600, 0, 3600):
            t = np.concatenate([np.arange(a, b, 0.1) for a, b in zip(m["trials"]["start"] + sh, m["trials"]["stop"] + sh)])
            t = t[(t > 0) & (t < m["duration"])]
            row[sh] = np.mean(ls_hfo.state_of(t, st) == "Non-REM") if len(t) else np.nan
        rows.append(row)
tc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"fraction of trial time scored NREM over {len(tc)} recordings, mean: true {tc[0].mean():.3f}, "
      f"trials shifted -1 h {tc[-3600].mean():.3f}, +1 h {tc[3600].mean():.3f}")

Three checks that the streams share one clock, each with a contrast that an offset would destroy.

  1. Spikes and LFP: the phase of the 120-200 Hz band at each spike is most consistent at zero shift and falls off within 5 to 10 ms, about one cycle. This holds for the hippocampal units inside CA1 ripples (32 of 39 recordings peak within +-2 ms) and for the LS units in high-power epochs (75 of 78). The 7 hippocampal recordings that peak elsewhere are all from DT5 (peaks at -20 to +10 ms), and the 3 LS recordings are two DT2 recordings and one DT9 recording. This check supports a common clock in most recordings and does not establish it in those 10.
  2. Sleep states and LFP: CA1 ripples are about 9 times as frequent in NREM as in WAKE with the states as stored, and about 2 times with the state table shifted by 10 min.
  3. Trials and states: 1.7% of trial time is scored NREM, against 31 to 39% with the trials shifted by 1 h.

The data are consistent with one clock for spikes, LFP, sleep states and trials.

dataset-composition¶

LS was recorded in 6 rats, with 1989 LS neurons; 37 recordings had CA1 and LS and 25 had CA3 and LS recorded simultaneously; LS HFO rates come from 89 recordings and CA1 ripple rates from 53.

In [7]:
def has_units(r, region):
    loc = r["meta"]["units"]["location"]
    return loc is not None and region in set(loc)

def has_el(r, region):
    return region in set(r["meta"]["el_location"])

fig1c-hfo-each-animal¶

Transient 120-180 Hz HFOs occur in LS in each of the 6 animals, with a robust increase in the firing probability of LS neurons at the events.

Spike probability is the number of spikes in +-10 ms of the event time (the 20 bins of 1 ms from -10 to +10 ms), per event and neuron, against as many uniformly random times in the same recording. A variant compares the same window with each neuron's firing 50 to 100 ms before and after the same events.

In [8]:
# fig1c-hfo-each-animal: frequency and HFO-triggered LS firing by animal
rng = np.random.default_rng(102)
rows, curves, flank_rows = [], {}, []
for subj in animals:
    freqs, ev_p, rnd_p, fl_p, n_events, peth_sum, peth_rnd = [], [], [], [], 0, 0, 0
    for r in [r for r in R if r["meta"]["subject"] == subj]:
        e = r["ls_events"]
        freqs.append(e["frequency"])
        n_events += len(e["peak"])
        units = ls_hfo.sorted_spikes(r, "ls")
        if len(e["peak"]) == 0 or not units:
            continue
        rnd_t = rng.uniform(0.2, r["meta"]["duration"] - 0.2, len(e["peak"]))
        for s in units.values():
            pe, pr = ls_hfo.peth(s, e["peak"]), ls_hfo.peth(s, rnd_t)
            ev_p.append(pe[90:110].sum())   # +-10 ms around the event time (1 ms bins)
            rnd_p.append(pr[90:110].sum())
            fl_p.append((pe[:50].sum() + pe[150:].sum()) / 100 * 20)   # 50-100 ms on each side, scaled to 20 bins
            peth_sum = peth_sum + pe
            peth_rnd = peth_rnd + pr
    d = np.array(ev_p) - np.array(rnd_p)
    dfl = np.array(ev_p) - np.array(fl_p)
    flank_rows.append({"animal": subj, "LS neurons": len(dfl), "P(spike) +-10 ms at HFO": round(np.mean(ev_p), 4),
                       "flanks 50-100 ms": round(np.mean(fl_p), 4), "difference": round(dfl.mean(), 4),
                       "SEM": round(dfl.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(dfl)), 4),
                       "difference / SEM": round(dfl.mean() / (dfl.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(dfl))), 1)})
    f = np.concatenate(freqs)
    curves[subj] = (peth_sum / len(ev_p), peth_rnd / len(ev_p))
    rows.append({"animal": subj, "HFOs": n_events, "median freq (Hz)": round(np.nanmedian(f), 1),
                 "LS neurons": len(ev_p), "P(spike) +-10 ms at HFO": round(np.mean(ev_p), 4),
                 "at random times": round(np.mean(rnd_p), 4), "difference": round(d.mean(), 4),
                 "SEM": round(d.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(d)), 4), "difference / SEM": round(d.mean() / (d.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(d))), 1)})
f1c = pd.DataFrame(rows)
f1c["freq in 120-180"] = f1c["median freq (Hz)"].between(120, 180)
f1c["above 3 SEM"] = f1c["difference / SEM"] > 3
print(f1c.to_string(index=False))
print("animals meeting both:", int((f1c["freq in 120-180"] & f1c["above 3 SEM"]).sum()), "of", len(f1c))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(animals), figsize=(15, 2.6), sharey=False)
lag = np.arange(-99.5, 100, 1)
for ax, subj in zip(axes, animals):
    ax.plot(lag, curves[subj][0], "k", lw=1, label="HFO")
    ax.plot(lag, curves[subj][1], "r", lw=1, label="random")
    ax.set_title(subj); ax.set_xlabel("ms from HFO")
axes[0].set_ylabel("spikes per event per 1 ms bin"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("plotted range (spikes per event per bin):", {s: (round(float(min(c[0].min(), c[1].min())), 4), round(float(max(c[0].max(), c[1].max())), 4)) for s, c in curves.items()})

# Variant (does not change the outcome): the same window against each neuron's own firing 50 to 100 ms
# before and after the same events, a baseline taken in the same moments as the events.

print("animals above 3 SEM against the flanks:", int((f1c_flank["difference / SEM"] > 3).sum()), "of", len(f1c_flank))

Variants that do not change the outcome: only the events in NREM, and only the events with a CA1 ripple within 25 ms (animals without states or hippocampal channels drop out).

In [9]:
# Variant (does not change the outcome): NREM events only, and events with a CA1 ripple within 25 ms.
rng = np.random.default_rng(1021)
def triggered(sel_fn):
    out = {}
    for subj in animals:
        d = []
        for r in [r for r in R if r["meta"]["subject"] == subj]:
            e = r["ls_events"]
            t = e["peak"][sel_fn(r, e)]
            units = ls_hfo.sorted_spikes(r, "ls")
            if len(t) < 5 or not units:
                continue
            rnd_t = rng.uniform(0.2, r["meta"]["duration"] - 0.2, len(t))
            d += [ls_hfo.peth(s, t)[90:110].sum() - ls_hfo.peth(s, rnd_t)[90:110].sum() for s in units.values()]
        d = np.array(d)
        out[subj] = (len(d), round(d.mean(), 4) if len(d) else None, round(d.mean() / (d.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(d))), 1) if len(d) > 2 else None)
    return out
def coupled(r, e):
    if "hpc_events" not in r:
        return np.zeros(len(e["peak"]), bool)
    rp = np.sort(r["hpc_events"]["peak"])
    k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(rp, e["peak"]), 1, max(len(rp) - 1, 1))
    near = np.minimum(np.abs(e["peak"] - rp[k - 1]), np.abs(e["peak"] - rp[np.minimum(k, len(rp) - 1)])) if len(rp) else np.full(len(e["peak"]), np.inf)
    return near <= 0.025
print("NREM events only (neurons, mean difference, difference/SEM):", triggered(lambda r, e: e["state"] == "Non-REM"))
print("events with a CA1 ripple within 25 ms:", triggered(coupled))

NREM events only (neurons, mean difference, difference/SEM): {'DT1': (0, None, None), 'DT2': (158, np.float64(0.0384), np.float64(3.3)), 'DT5': (378, np.float64(-0.0026), np.float64(-0.4)), 'DT7': (51, np.float64(-0.0026), np.float64(-0.7)), 'DT8': (0, None, None), 'DT9': (478, np.float64(0.0092), np.float64(3.9))}

events with a CA1 ripple within 25 ms: {'DT1': (0, None, None), 'DT2': (396, np.float64(0.0286), np.float64(1.4)), 'DT5': (309, np.float64(0.0803), np.float64(2.0)), 'DT7': (51, np.float64(-0.0047), np.float64(-1.7)), 'DT8': (296, np.float64(-0.0087), np.float64(-5.7)), 'DT9': (352, np.float64(0.0117), np.float64(4.2))}

Result: not reproduced. Every animal's detected events have a median frequency of 152 to 158 Hz, inside 120 to 180 Hz, but LS firing within +-10 ms of the events exceeds firing at random times by more than 3 SEM in DT1 only (6.0 SEM). In DT2 and DT5 it is higher by 1.3 and 1.4 SEM, and in DT7, DT8 and DT9 it is lower (-3.4, -4.6 and -1.4 SEM). With NREM events only, DT2 (3.3 SEM) and DT9 (3.9 SEM) pass; with ripple-coupled events, DT9 passes (4.2 SEM). On the re-referenced channel (see the check after fig5f) no animal passes (largest 1.5 SEM, DT2; DT8 -4.4 SEM). Random times are a baseline that mixes states. Against each neuron's firing 50 to 100 ms before and after the same events, firing at the events is higher in DT1, DT2, DT5 and DT9 (DT9 0.0151 against 0.0145) and lower in DT7 and DT8, and exceeds 3 SEM only in DT1 (5.2 SEM; DT2 1.6, DT5 1.7, DT9 0.5). In DT2 and DT5 the differences are large (0.024 and 0.037) but vary widely across neurons. The test does not show raised LS firing at the events outside DT1; it does not show that the events lack it.

figs1-participation¶

On average 16% of LS neurons take part in a given HFO, firing an average of 0.23 spikes per event.

In [11]:
# figs1-participation
frac_ev, spk_ev, per_rec = [], [], []
for r in R:
    units = ls_hfo.sorted_spikes(r, "ls")
    e = r["ls_events"]
    if not units or len(e["peak"]) == 0:
        continue
    C = np.array([ls_hfo.counts_in(s, e["start"], e["stop"]) for s in units.values()])  # neurons x events
    frac_ev.append((C > 0).mean(axis=0))
    spk_ev.append(C.ravel())
    per_rec.append({"file": r["path"].split("/")[1][:30], "neurons": len(units), "events": C.shape[1],
                    "fraction": (C > 0).mean(), "spikes": C.mean()})
per_rec = pd.DataFrame(per_rec)
fa, sa = np.concatenate(frac_ev).mean(), np.concatenate(spk_ev).mean()
print(f"(a) pooled over {sum(len(x) for x in frac_ev)} events: fraction of LS neurons firing {fa:.3f}, spikes per neuron per event {sa:.3f}")
print(f"(b) mean of {len(per_rec)} recordings: fraction {per_rec.fraction.mean():.3f}, spikes {per_rec.spikes.mean():.3f}")
print("paper: 0.16 (tolerance 0.016) and 0.23 (0.023)")
print(f"ratio to the paper's values: fraction {fa / 0.16:.2f} (pooled), {per_rec.fraction.mean() / 0.16:.2f} (recordings);"
      f" spikes {sa / 0.23:.2f} (pooled), {per_rec.spikes.mean() / 0.23:.2f} (recordings)")
print(f"per-recording fraction: median {per_rec.fraction.median():.3f}, range {per_rec.fraction.min():.3f} to {per_rec.fraction.max():.3f}")

Result: not reproduced. Pooled over events, 2.7% of LS neurons fire in an HFO, with 0.051 spikes per neuron per event; the mean over recordings gives 3.5% and 0.068. The fraction is 0.17 (pooled) to 0.22 (recordings) of the paper's value, and the spike count 0.22 to 0.30 of it. The highest recording reaches 18.2%. On the re-referenced channel the pooled values are 4.5% and 0.060.

fig1d-phase-locking¶

The vast majority of LS neurons (1840 of 1989, 92%) are significantly phase-locked to the 120-200 Hz band (Rayleigh P < 0.05), with a strong preference for the trough of each cycle.

The phase is taken on each recording's HFO detection channel; the paper does not say which channel it used.

In [12]:
# fig1d-phase-locking
pl = pd.DataFrame([{"animal": r["meta"]["subject"], **{k: p[k] for k in ("n", "p", "r", "phase")},
                    "r_null": np.nanmean(p["r_null"])} for r in R for p in r["phase_locking"]])
tested = pl[pl.n > 50]
sig = tested[tested.p < 0.05]
print(f"LS neurons: {len(pl)}; with more than 50 spikes in high-power epochs: {len(tested)}; significant (Rayleigh p < 0.05): {len(sig)}")
print(f"fraction significant: (a) of tested {len(sig) / len(tested):.3f}; (b) of all LS neurons {len(sig) / len(pl):.3f}  (paper 0.925, tolerance 0.0925)")
print(f"resultant length of tested neurons: median {tested.r.median():.3f}; with the phase circularly shifted: median {tested.r_null.median():.3f}")
mean_dir = np.angle(np.exp(1j * sig.phase).mean())
rt = len(sig) * np.abs(np.exp(1j * sig.phase).mean())
p_pref = np.exp(np.sqrt(1 + 4 * len(sig) + 4 * (len(sig) ** 2 - rt ** 2)) - (1 + 2 * len(sig)))
print(f"preferred phases of significant neurons: circular mean {np.degrees(mean_dir) % 360:.1f} deg (trough = 180),"
      f" resultant {np.abs(np.exp(1j * sig.phase).mean()):.3f}, Rayleigh p = {p_pref:.2g}")
print(f"within 45 deg of the trough: {abs(abs(np.degrees(mean_dir)) - 180) <= 45}")
print("by animal:")
print(tested.groupby("animal").apply(lambda d: pd.Series({"tested": len(d), "significant": int((d.p < 0.05).sum()),
      "fraction": round((d.p < 0.05).mean(), 3), "median r": round(d.r.median(), 3),
      "mean phase (deg)": round(np.degrees(np.angle(np.exp(1j * d.phase[d.p < 0.05]).mean())) % 360, 1)})).to_string())

In [13]:
# Check: could the trough preference come from each unit's own spikes in the LFP? The phase is taken
# again on an LS channel on another shank than the unit's: the detection channel for units on other
# shanks, and for units on the detection shank the LS channel with the highest 120-200 Hz SD on
# another shank. Recordings with LS channels on one shank only drop out.
def circ_summary(ph):
    c = np.exp(1j * np.asarray(ph)).mean()
    n = len(ph)
    R_ = n * np.abs(c)
    p_ = np.exp(np.sqrt(1 + 4 * n + 4 * (n ** 2 - R_ ** 2)) - (1 + 2 * n))
    return np.degrees(np.angle(c)) % 360, np.abs(c), p_

rows = []
for r in R:
    grp = r["meta"]["units"]["group"]
    if grp is None or "phase_locking_other" not in r:
        continue
    for k, i in enumerate(r["ls_units"]):
        same = grp[i] == r["channel_groups"]["ls"]
        d_, o_ = r["phase_locking"][k], r["phase_locking_other"][k]
        off = o_ if same else d_
        rows.append({"animal": r["meta"]["subject"], "on detection shank": same,
                     "n_det": d_["n"], "p_det": d_["p"], "r_det": d_["r"], "ph_det": d_["phase"],
                     "n_off": off["n"], "p_off": off["p"], "r_off": off["r"], "ph_off": off["phase"]})
ps = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"LS units in recordings with LS channels on two or more shanks: {len(ps)} of {len(pl)}")
for label, d in (("units on the detection shank, detection channel", ps[ps["on detection shank"]].rename(columns=lambda c: c.replace("_det", ""))),
                 ("units on other shanks, detection channel", ps[~ps["on detection shank"]].rename(columns=lambda c: c.replace("_det", ""))),
                 ("all units, phase from another shank", ps.rename(columns=lambda c: c.replace("_off", "")))):
    t_ = d[d.n > 50]
    s_ = t_[t_.p < 0.05]
    mdeg, res_, pp_ = circ_summary(s_.ph) if len(s_) else (np.nan, np.nan, np.nan)
    print(f"{label}: tested {len(t_)}, significant {len(s_)} ({len(s_) / max(len(t_), 1):.3f}); median resultant {t_.r.median():.3f};"
          f" above 0.6: {(t_.r > 0.6).sum()}; preferred phase {mdeg:.1f} deg (resultant {res_:.3f}, Rayleigh p = {pp_:.2g})")
t_ = ps[ps.n_off > 50]
print("phase from another shank, by animal:")
print(t_.groupby("animal").apply(lambda d: pd.Series({"tested": len(d), "fraction": round((d.p_off < 0.05).mean(), 3),
      "mean phase (deg)": round(circ_summary(d.ph_off[d.p_off < 0.05])[0], 1) if (d.p_off < 0.05).any() else np.nan})).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. 1151 of 2046 tested LS neurons (56.3%) are significantly phase-locked, 47.0% of all 2448; the paper reports 92.5%. The trough preference holds: the preferred phases of significant neurons centre on 189 degrees (resultant 0.755; the Rayleigh p underflows to 0). Fractions range from 5.7% (DT7) to 70.4% (DT5) by animal. Median resultant lengths are 0.124 for the data and 0.048 with the phase circularly shifted.

The trough preference does not come from each unit's own spikes in the LFP. With the phase taken on an LS channel on another shank than the unit's, 1048 of 2003 tested neurons (52.3%) are locked, with preferred phases centred on 189.7 degrees (resultant 0.743), and 44 have a resultant above 0.6. Locking is stronger for the units on the detection shank (76.4% of 461, median resultant 0.191) than for those on other shanks (51.4% of 1550, 0.110), so part of the locking measured on the unit's own shank may come from its spikes or from its distance to the channel.

fig1f-shorter-than-ripples and fig1g-slower-than-ripples¶

LS HFOs are shorter than CA1 ripples from the same animals (27 +- 9 against 31 +- 14 ms; rank-sum P < 0.01).

LS HFOs are slower in frequency than CA1 ripples (147 +- 5.7 against 159 +- 8 Hz; rank-sum P < 0.01).

Result: fig1f-shorter-than-ripples reproduced. LS HFOs last 33.9 +- 25.0 ms and CA1 ripples 38.3 +- 23.7 ms, both inside the tolerances of the paper's SDs, and LS HFOs are shorter (medians 23.2 and 32.0 ms; the rank-sum p underflows to 0, as it does for any difference over 56,871 and 230,161 events). The means are 6 to 7 ms above the paper's. In four of five animals LS HFOs are significantly shorter; in DT8 they are not (27.5 against 28.0 ms, p = 0.83). With NREM events only, the means are 38.0 and 38.4 ms (p = 8.3e-103), and on the re-referenced channel 38.2 and 38.3 ms, so the 4 ms gap in the means is not seen in NREM events or on the re-referenced channel.

Result: fig1g-slower-than-ripples not reproduced. LS HFOs have a mean frequency of 153.6 +- 8.3 Hz and CA1 ripples 150.8 +- 9.2 Hz: the LS events are faster, the reverse of the claim, and both means are outside the tolerances (147 +- 5.7 and 159 +- 8). LS events are faster in four of five animals. With NREM events only, LS are slower by 0.8 Hz (150.3 against 151.1 Hz). On the re-referenced channel LS events are faster (156.3 against 150.8 Hz).

Result: not reproduced. Over 67,186 events the Pearson correlation is small but significant (r = 0.056, p = 2.4e-47; Spearman rho = 0.123). By animal, r is -0.009 to 0.080, significant in four of six; with NREM events only, r = 0.028 (p = 7.3e-05). The outcome follows the criterion's test; the correlation is negligible in size (r = 0.056 explains 0.3% of the variance) and is significant because of the event count. The paper does not name its test.

fig2-confined-to-ls¶

HFO events are seen only at recording sites within LS, not at sites in neighbouring structures.

DT7 has probes that span cingulate cortex (acg), corpus callosum (cc), medial septum (ms) and fimbria (sFi) with LS. For each channel, the 120-200 Hz power within +-20 ms of the LS HFO times in up to 30 min of all channels, divided by the power at random times.

Result: not reproduced. Five recordings, all from DT7 (the only animal whose files label electrodes outside LS and the hippocampus), have at least 20 HFOs in the block. LS channels have the highest ratio in two: 2017-03-18 (5.38 against 5.31 for cingulate cortex) and 2017-03-21 (8.25 against 8.05 for medial septum). In the other three, medial septum (6.05 against 5.18), corpus callosum (50.1 against 42.0) or fimbria (72.1 against 64.8) channels are higher. With each channel re-referenced to the median of its shank and the re-referenced LS events as triggers, four recordings have at least 20 events and LS is highest in two; medial septum channels are higher in the other two (4.00 against 3.09 and 4.21 against 3.65). The detected events reach channels outside LS at similar or larger relative power. The test rests on one animal.

fig2ef-intermediate-ls (blocked)¶

HFO power and the proportion of phase-locked neurons are highest in intermediate LS and taper towards its dorsal and ventral borders.

The claim is blocked: it needs each recording's depth relative to the borders of LS, which the paper took from histology. The session names carry drive depths in um (one in DT1, two in the other animals, without saying which drive holds the LS probe). For the record, the HFO band SD of the detection channel, the LS HFO rate and the fraction of tested LS neurons that are phase-locked are shown against each depth within each animal.

In [17]:
# fig2ef-intermediate-ls (blocked): drive depth in the session name against HFO power and locking
import re
rows = []
for r in R:
    name = r["path"].split("/")[1]
    depths = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r"(\d+)um", name)]
    t_ = [p_ for p_ in r["phase_locking"] if p_["n"] > 50]
    rows.append({"animal": r["meta"]["subject"], "depth 1": depths[0], "depth 2": depths[1] if len(depths) > 1 else np.nan,
                 "band SD (uV)": r["channel_stats"]["band_sd"][r["channels"]["ls"]] * r["meta"]["lfp_conversion"] * 1e6,
                 "HFO rate (/min)": 60 * len(r["ls_events"]["peak"]) / r["meta"]["duration"],
                 "tested": len(t_), "locked fraction": np.mean([p_["p"] < 0.05 for p_ in t_]) if len(t_) >= 5 else np.nan})
dp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out = []
for subj, d in dp.groupby("animal"):
    for dcol in ("depth 1", "depth 2"):
        if d[dcol].nunique() < 3:
            continue
        row = {"animal": subj, "depth": dcol, "recordings": len(d), "range (um)": f"{d[dcol].min():.0f}-{d[dcol].max():.0f}"}
        for v in ("band SD (uV)", "HFO rate (/min)", "locked fraction"):
            k = d[[dcol, v]].dropna()
            row[f"rho {v}"] = round(stats.spearmanr(k[dcol], k[v]).statistic, 2) if len(k) >= 4 else np.nan
            # where the largest value falls in the depth range (0 = shallowest, 1 = deepest)
            row[f"argmax {v}"] = round((k.loc[k[v].idxmax(), dcol] - k[dcol].min()) / (k[dcol].max() - k[dcol].min()), 2) if len(k) >= 4 and k[dcol].max() > k[dcol].min() else np.nan
        out.append(row)
print(pd.DataFrame(out).to_string(index=False))
print("recordings by animal with at least 5 tested neurons:", dp.dropna(subset=["locked fraction"]).groupby("animal").size().to_dict())

Result: blocked (metadata insufficient). Shown for the record. Within animals, the rank correlations with depth are -0.61 to 0.41 for the HFO band SD and -0.84 to 0.36 for the locked fraction. The band SD is largest at the shallowest or deepest recording (relative position at most 0.08 or at least 0.98) in 9 of 11 animal and depth series; the locked fraction peaks inside the range (relative position 0.19 to 0.84) in 5 of 9. Without the LS borders, and without knowing which drive holds the LS probe, these do not test the claim.

LS pairs: fig4b-pre-post-unchanged, fig4b-hfo-above-behav, fig4d-compression¶

The co-activation of LS neuron pairs during HFOs (excess correlation) is not modulated by waking experience on a familiar maze (PRE against POST, rank-sum P = 0.36).

Excess correlations during HFOs (PRE and POST) are higher than during maze traversal (rank-sum P < 0.001), and those of PRE and POST HFOs exceed chance from spikes jittered by +-200 ms (P < 0.01).

Cross-correlograms of LS pairs during HFOs correlate with those during traversal above chance up to about 20-fold temporal compression (P < 0.01), similarly for PRE and POST (P > 0.01 for all compression factors).

The pair selection of the criteria (pairs on different shanks with more than 5 spike pairs within +-200 ms in each epoch) is applied first; it decides which of these claims have enough data.

In [18]:
# Pairs of LS neurons on different shanks: CCGs of spikes inside LS HFOs (PRE, POST) and inside trials (BEHAV).
rng = np.random.default_rng(109)
FACTORS = [1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50]
NB = 400                       # bins of 1 ms on each side
W200 = slice(NB - 200, NB + 201)

def warp_corr(c_hfo, c_beh, factor):
    """Correlation of the BEHAV CCG over +-120 ms with the HFO CCG over +-120/factor ms,
    interpolated to the same 241 points."""
    lags = np.arange(-NB, NB + 1)
    x = np.linspace(-120 / factor, 120 / factor, 241)
    a = np.interp(x, lags, c_hfo)
    b = c_beh[NB - 120:NB + 121]
    if a.std() == 0 or b.std() == 0:
        return np.nan
    return np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1]

pair_rows, comp_rows, kept_sessions = [], [], 0
t_start = time.time()
for r in R:
    m = r["meta"]
    units = ls_hfo.sorted_spikes(r, "ls")
    if m["epochs"] is None or m["trials"] is None or len(units) < 2 or m["units"]["group"] is None:
        continue
    e = r["ls_events"]
    order = np.argsort(e["start"])
    es, ee, ep = e["start"][order], e["stop"][order], e["peak"][order]
    pre = ep < m["epochs"]["stop"][0]
    post = ep >= m["epochs"]["start"][2]
    to = np.argsort(m["trials"]["start"])
    ts, tt = m["trials"]["start"][to], m["trials"]["stop"][to]
    sp = {"PRE": {}, "BEHAV": {}, "POST": {}}
    for i, s in units.items():
        sp["PRE"][i] = ls_hfo.in_intervals(s, es[pre], ee[pre])
        sp["POST"][i] = ls_hfo.in_intervals(s, es[post], ee[post])
        sp["BEHAV"][i] = ls_hfo.in_intervals(s, ts, tt)
    grp = m["units"]["group"]
    ids = list(units)
    n_pairs = 0
    for a_ in range(len(ids)):
        for b_ in range(a_ + 1, len(ids)):
            i, j = ids[a_], ids[b_]
            if grp[i] == grp[j]:
                continue
            C = {k: ls_hfo.ccg(sp[k][i], sp[k][j], half=NB / 1000) for k in sp}
            if any(C[k][W200].sum() <= 5 for k in C):
                continue
            row = {"file": r["path"].split("/")[1][:30], "subject": m["subject"]}
            for k in C:
                cn = C[k] / np.sqrt(len(sp[k][i]) * len(sp[k][j]))
                row[k] = ls_hfo.excess_correlation(cn)
                ji = np.sort(sp[k][i] + rng.uniform(-0.2, 0.2, len(sp[k][i])))
                jj = np.sort(sp[k][j] + rng.uniform(-0.2, 0.2, len(sp[k][j])))
                row[k + "_jitter"] = ls_hfo.excess_correlation(ls_hfo.ccg(ji, jj, half=NB / 1000) / np.sqrt(len(ji) * len(jj)))
                row["bias_" + k] = cn[NB + 1:NB + 201].sum() - cn[NB - 200:NB].sum()
                C[k] = cn
            for k in ("PRE", "POST"):
                shift = rng.integers(1, 2 * NB)
                for fct in FACTORS:
                    comp_rows.append({"file": row["file"], "epoch": k, "factor": fct,
                                      "corr": warp_corr(C[k], C["BEHAV"], fct),
                                      "chance": warp_corr(np.roll(C[k], shift), C["BEHAV"], fct)})
            pair_rows.append(row)
            n_pairs += 1
    kept_sessions += n_pairs > 0
pairs = pd.DataFrame(pair_rows)
comp = pd.DataFrame(comp_rows)
print(f"pairs kept: {len(pairs)} in {kept_sessions} recordings (paper 7,172 pairs in 53 sessions); {time.time() - t_start:.0f} s")
print("pairs by animal:", pairs.subject.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
print(pairs[["PRE", "BEHAV", "POST", "PRE_jitter", "BEHAV_jitter", "POST_jitter"]].describe().round(4).to_string())

Only 106 pairs from 10 recordings in 3 animals pass the selection, against 7,172 pairs in 53 sessions in the paper. Few LS spikes fall inside the detected HFOs (see figs1-participation), so most pairs have 5 or fewer spike pairs within +-200 ms in PRE or POST. The shortfall comes from this attempt's detection, not from the dandiset, which holds the spikes, epochs and trials of these recordings. The pair-level tests below use these 106 pairs and have far less power than the paper's. The per-session claims are blocked: 7 recordings have at least 5 pairs (fig4-sessions-few-change) and 4 have at least 10 (fig4c-temporal-bias); their outputs are printed for the record.

Result: fig4d-compression not reproduced. PRE correlations exceed chance at factors 1 and 2 only, POST at 1, 2, 4 and 20. PRE and POST do not differ at any factor (smallest p = 0.038). The number of pairs with a defined correlation falls from 59 (PRE) and 77 (POST) at factor 1 to 5 and 11 at factor 50, as the HFO correlogram is empty in the narrow windows; at factor 4, PRE rests on 24 pairs (p = 0.18). Chance uses one circular shift per pair for all factors.

figs2-post-rate-increase¶

Firing rates increase during post-behavior NREM sleep in CA1, CA3 and LS.

In [23]:
# figs2-post-rate-increase
rows = []
for r in R + skipped:
    m = r["meta"]
    if m["states"] is None or m["epochs"] is None or m["units"]["location"] is None:
        continue
    st = m["states"]
    nrem = st["label"] == "Non-REM"
    def nrem_within(a, b):
        s0, s1 = np.clip(st["start"][nrem], a, b), np.clip(st["stop"][nrem], a, b)
        keep = s1 > s0
        return s0[keep], s1[keep]
    pre_iv = nrem_within(m["epochs"]["start"][0], m["epochs"]["stop"][0])
    post_iv = nrem_within(m["epochs"]["start"][2], m["epochs"]["stop"][2])
    dpre, dpost = (pre_iv[1] - pre_iv[0]).sum(), (post_iv[1] - post_iv[0]).sum()
    if dpre < 60 or dpost < 60:
        continue
    o1, o2 = np.argsort(pre_iv[0]), np.argsort(post_iv[0])
    for i, s in enumerate(m["units"]["spikes"]):
        s = np.sort(s)
        rows.append({"region": m["units"]["location"][i], "subject": m["subject"],
                     "pre": ls_hfo.counts_in(s, pre_iv[0][o1], pre_iv[1][o1]).sum() / dpre,
                     "post": ls_hfo.counts_in(s, post_iv[0][o2], post_iv[1][o2]).sum() / dpost})
rates_pp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out = []
for g in ("hpc", "ca3", "ls"):
    d = rates_pp[(rates_pp.region == g) & ((rates_pp.pre > 0) | (rates_pp.post > 0))]
    w = stats.wilcoxon(d.post, d.pre)
    out.append({"region": g, "units": len(d), "recordings": None, "median PRE (Hz)": round(d.pre.median(), 3),
                "median POST (Hz)": round(d.post.median(), 3),
                "median POST/PRE": round(np.median((d.post + 1e-3) / (d.pre + 1e-3)), 3), "Wilcoxon p": w.pvalue})
print(pd.DataFrame(out).drop(columns="recordings").to_string(index=False))
print("by animal, median POST/PRE:")
print(rates_pp[(rates_pp.pre > 0) | (rates_pp.post > 0)].assign(ratio=lambda d: (d.post + 1e-3) / (d.pre + 1e-3))
      .groupby(["region", "subject"]).ratio.agg(["count", "median"]).round(3).to_string())

fig5b-nrem-and-rates¶

LS HFOs occur primarily during NREM sleep, and their rates are lower than those of hippocampal SPW-Rs.

fig5d-lag and fig5e-state-coupling¶

LS HFOs are reliably coupled to CA1 ripples, with a median peak-to-peak lag of 6.4 +- 4.2 ms, CA1 leading LS.

HPC-LS coupling is stronger in NREM sleep than in waking; the fraction of LS HFOs within +-25 ms of a CA1 ripple is 0.3 in NREM and 0.15 in WAKE (P < 6.6e-6).

In [25]:
# fig5d-lag and fig5e-state-coupling
def nearest(t, ref):
    ref = np.sort(ref)
    if len(ref) == 0:
        return np.full(len(t), np.nan)
    k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(ref, t), 1, len(ref) - 1) if len(ref) > 1 else np.zeros(len(t), int)
    lo, hi = ref[np.maximum(k - 1, 0)], ref[k]
    return np.where(np.abs(t - lo) <= np.abs(t - hi), t - lo, t - hi)   # t minus the nearest ref

Result: fig5d-lag not reproduced. LS HFOs are coupled to CA1 ripples: the pooled correlogram peaks at 0 ms, 166 SD above its flanks. The lag is 0.00 ms under both readings, outside 6.4 +- 4.2 ms, and LS follows CA1 in only 33.5% of pairs; 34.8% of the coupled pairs fall on the same sample (71% in DT8, 7% in DT9). Without the pairs within 1 ms the pooled median is 3.2 ms, LS after CA1 in 55%, but by animal it is -3.2 (DT2), -5.6 (DT5), -6.4 (DT7), 1.6 (DT8) and 8.0 ms (DT9), so LS leads in three animals. Over all pairs, DT9's median of recording medians is 3.8 ms, inside the tolerance (2.2 to 10.6 ms); the other four animals give 0.0 ms. On the re-referenced channel, where 4.1% of pairs fall on the same sample, the coupling remains (53.4 SD at 0 ms) and the lag is 0.00 ms (a) and 0.80 ms (b), LS after CA1 in 52%, still outside the tolerance. The coupling part of the claim holds and the lag part does not. The criterion requires the lag within tolerance under one reading and defines no partial outcome, so the claim is not reproduced.

Result: fig5e-state-coupling not reproduced. Over 25 recordings, the fraction of LS HFOs within 25 ms of a CA1 ripple is 0.199 in NREM and 0.116 in WAKE (two-sample t-test p = 0.089); pooled, 0.088 and 0.041. The direction matches the paper, but the difference is not significant and the values are below 0.3 and 0.15. Chance (ripple times shifted by 1 s) is 0.019 and 0.005. On the re-referenced channel, over 16 recordings, 0.118 and 0.085 (p = 0.43).

fig5f-ripple-triggered-firing and fig5f-no-phase-coherence¶

LS firing around CA1 ripples is higher during NREM than during waking.

CA1-LS phase coherence in the 120-180 Hz band around CA1 ripples does not differ from that of randomly jittered windows, so LS does not inherit the ripple wave by wave.

Result: fig5f-ripple-triggered-firing not reproduced. Over 978 LS neurons, the rate within 25 ms of CA1 ripples is 1.39 Hz in NREM and 1.33 Hz in WAKE (paired t-test p = 0.24). Divided by each neuron's rate in the same state, WAKE is higher (1.56 against 1.34, p = 0.00016).

Result: fig5f-no-phase-coherence not reproduced. The CA1-LS phase-locking value at the ripple time is 0.405, against 0.202 +- 0.007 for jittered windows (31 SD above), and 90 of 125 lags within +-50 ms exceed the bound. It is higher at ripples in 70 of 71 recordings. The jittered value itself is high: with a median of 1722 ripples per recording, random phase differences would give about 0.021, and the jittered value per recording is 0.030 to 0.602 (median 0.134). The two channels keep a phase relation outside ripples too, a signal common to both. On the re-referenced LS channel the value at ripples is 0.164 against 0.074 +- 0.004 jittered (23.9 SD above, higher in 60 of 71 recordings): re-referencing on the shank lowers both, and the coherence at ripples stays above chance.

Check: LS events on a re-referenced channel¶

Several outputs above point to a 120-200 Hz signal shared by the LS detection channel and the hippocampal channel: a third of the coupled LS events fall on the same sample as the CA1 ripple, and the CA1-LS phase-locking value at jittered times is far above that of random phases. A signal common to every channel, such as the reference, would do this. Here the detection channel is re-referenced to the LS channel on its own shank with the lowest 120-200 Hz SD, which removes what is common to the shank, and events are detected again with the same parameters. The measures of the HFO claims are repeated on these events. This check is not in the paper's Methods and does not decide an outcome; it shows how much of each result rests on the shared signal.

On the re-referenced channel the share of coupled LS events on the same sample as the CA1 ripple falls from 34.8% to 4.1%, so most of those events came from a signal common to the shank. The other measures do not move towards the paper's: no animal shows LS firing at the events more than 3 SEM above random times, the lag stays at 0 to 0.8 ms, NREM rates are not above WAKE, and coherence at ripples stays above chance. Event counts change a lot (DT5 4,032 to 34,492; DT8 2,757 to 1,243), so the event set depends on the referencing, which the paper does not describe. No outcome is changed by this check.

fig6-optogenetic-hfos (blocked)¶

Optogenetic activation of LS GABAergic neurons with a Gaussian light waveform induces local oscillations of about 140 Hz.

The two rats used for optogenetics are not among the 6 subjects of the dandiset (see the data check), and no file holds an optogenetic series. The cell below searches the archive for other dandisets by the same authors.

fig7e-ca1-spikes, fig7e-state and fig7e-duration¶

The number of CA1 spikes in a SPW-R significantly predicts the number of spikes of 38% of LS neurons.

Brain state (WAKE or NREM) in which a SPW-R occurs significantly predicts the spike count of 26% of LS neurons.

The duration of hippocampal SPW-Rs significantly predicts the spike count of about 20% of LS neurons.

The model is fixed in the claims file (linear regression, 5-fold cross-validated MSE, 100 shuffles). Reading (a) calls a neuron significant when its MSE is below the 5th percentile of the shuffles, reading (b) when a t-test of the shuffles against it gives p < 0.05. The chance rate tests one shuffle against the others.

In [30]:
# fig7e-ca1-spikes, fig7e-state, fig7e-duration: does a ripple feature predict an LS neuron's spike count?
N_SHUF = 100


def fig7_rows(rng, fixed_window=None):
    rows = []
    for r in R:
        if "hpc_events" not in r:
            continue
        ca1 = ls_hfo.sorted_spikes(r, "hpc")
        lsu = ls_hfo.sorted_spikes(r, "ls")
        e = r["hpc_events"]
        if not ca1 or not lsu or len(e["peak"]) < 100:
            continue
        win = (e["start"], e["stop"]) if fixed_window is None else (e["peak"] - fixed_window, e["peak"] + fixed_window)
        Y = np.array([ls_hfo.counts_in(s, *win) for s in lsu.values()]).T.astype(float)   # ripples x neurons
        keep_n = Y.sum(axis=0) >= 20
        if not keep_n.any():
            continue
        Y = Y[:, keep_n]
        n_ca1 = np.sum([ls_hfo.counts_in(s, e["start"], e["stop"]) for s in ca1.values()], axis=0).astype(float)
        feats = {"ca1_spikes": (n_ca1, np.ones(len(n_ca1), bool)), "duration": (e["duration"], np.ones(len(n_ca1), bool)),
                 "state": ((e["state"] == "Non-REM").astype(float), np.isin(e["state"], ["Non-REM", "Awake"]))}
        for name, (x, sel) in feats.items():
            if sel.sum() < 100 or np.unique(x[sel]).size < 2:
                continue
            xs, ys = x[sel], Y[sel]
            folds = rng.permutation(np.arange(len(xs)) % 5)
            X = np.column_stack([xs] + [rng.permutation(xs) for _ in range(N_SHUF)])
            mse = ls_hfo.cv_mse(ys, X, folds)               # neurons x (1 + shuffles)
            actual, shuf = mse[:, 0], mse[:, 1:]
            for k in range(len(actual)):
                s = shuf[k]
                # chance: shuffle 0 tested against the other shuffles
                c, cs = s[0], s[1:]
                tt = stats.ttest_1samp(s, actual[k])
                tc = stats.ttest_1samp(cs, c)
                rows.append({"feature": name, "subject": r["meta"]["subject"], "file": r["path"].split("/")[1][:30],
                             "z": (s.mean() - actual[k]) / s.std(ddof=1) if s.std() > 0 else np.nan,
                             "sig_a": actual[k] < np.percentile(s, 5), "sig_b": (tt.pvalue < 0.05) and actual[k] < s.mean(),
                             "chance_a": c < np.percentile(cs, 5), "chance_b": (tc.pvalue < 0.05) and c < cs.mean()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fig7_summary(f7):
    summary = []
    for name, d in f7.groupby("feature"):
        row = {"feature": name, "LS neurons": len(d), "recordings": d.file.nunique()}
        for rd in ("a", "b"):
            k, n, ch = d[f"sig_{rd}"].sum(), len(d), d[f"chance_{rd}"].mean()
            row[f"% ({rd})"] = round(100 * k / n, 1)
            row[f"chance % ({rd})"] = round(100 * ch, 1)
            row[f"binomial p vs chance ({rd})"] = stats.binomtest(int(k), n, max(ch, 1e-6), alternative="greater").pvalue
        summary.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(summary)


f7 = fig7_rows(np.random.default_rng(118))
f7s = fig7_summary(f7)
print(f7s.to_string(index=False))
print("paper: CA1 spikes 38%, state 26%, duration about 20%")
print("by animal, % significant under reading (a):")
print(f7.groupby(["feature", "subject"]).sig_a.agg(["count", "mean"]).assign(mean=lambda d: (100 * d["mean"]).round(1)).to_string())
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))
for j, (name, d) in enumerate(f7.groupby("feature")):
    ax.plot(j + np.random.default_rng(1181).uniform(-0.2, 0.2, len(d)), d.z.clip(-5, 20), "k.", ms=2)
    ax.set_xticks(range(f7.feature.nunique()), sorted(f7.feature.unique()))
ax.set_ylabel("SDs of shuffled MSE above actual (clipped -5 to 20)"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("z outside the axis (clipped):", int(((f7.z < -5) | (f7.z > 20)).sum()), "of", len(f7))

# Variant: spikes counted in a fixed +-25 ms window around the ripple time, so the count does not grow with duration.
f7v = fig7_rows(np.random.default_rng(1182), fixed_window=0.025)
print("variant, fixed +-25 ms window:")
print(fig7_summary(f7v).to_string(index=False))

Result: fig7e-ca1-spikes partially reproduced. The number of CA1 spikes predicts 79.4% of 880 LS neurons under reading (a) (chance 4.7%), above chance and far above the paper's 38%. Spikes are counted from ripple start to stop, so both the LS and the CA1 counts grow with the ripple's duration; with a fixed +-25 ms window, 24.7% under (a) (chance 5.6%). Reading (b) is not usable: its chance rate is 40.5% (88.4% significant), because a one-sample t-test of 99 shuffled MSEs against a single value is significant whenever that value lies a little away from their mean.

Result: fig7e-state partially reproduced. State predicts 34.3% of 813 LS neurons under (a) (chance 5.4%), above chance and above 26 +- 2.6%. With a fixed window, 34.9% (chance 6.0%). Under (b), 67.4% against a chance rate of 41.7%.

Result: fig7e-duration partially reproduced. Duration predicts 86.0% of 880 LS neurons under (a) (chance 5.9%), far above about 20%. Counting spikes from ripple start to stop makes the count grow with duration, which inflates this; with a fixed +-25 ms window it is 17.8% (chance 7.2%), just below the tolerance (18 to 22%). The fixed window is a variant and does not decide the outcome. Under (b), 93.2% against a chance rate of 41.1%.

fig7e-ca1-depth (blocked)¶

The mean depth within the CA1 pyramidal layer of the neurons active in a SPW-R predicts the spike count of 23% of LS neurons.

The depth of a CA1 neuron comes from its waveform amplitude across sites, and the units table holds no waveforms or channels (see the data check). Waveforms could only be re-extracted from wide-band data. The cell below lists the files that hold a series sampled above 5 kHz in acquisition, with their size and the hippocampal units they hold.

Result: blocked (data missing). 27 of 98 files hold a 20 kHz wide-band series: all 12 DT1 files, all 13 DT2 files and 2 DT9 files, which take 1.15 TB. Twelve of them (10 DT2, 2 DT9) hold hippocampal units, 1.00 TB of wide-band data, which would have to be streamed at about 556 MB/s to fit the 30 min run limit; for these recordings the claim is blocked by run time. The other 1579 of 2778 hippocampal units, including all of DT5 and DT7, have no wide-band data, and for them the waveforms are missing.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • The files hold no detected events, and the paper does not say which channels it used. LS HFOs and CA1 ripples are detected here on one channel each, chosen by a fixed rule, with the Methods' parameters and the buzcode detector's open details. The paper's noise channel is replaced by the EMG estimated from the LFP. LS firing at the detected events exceeds firing at random times, or before and after the events, by more than 3 SEM in one animal of six, participation is a sixth to a third of the paper's, and a third of the events coupled to ripples fall on the same sample as the ripple. Neither the detection channel nor the re-referenced one is shown to capture the paper's HFOs; most of the outcomes on HFOs follow from that.
  • A check added after the first verification: events detected on the LS channel re-referenced to another LS channel on its shank. It removes most LS events that fell on the same sample as a CA1 ripple (34.8% to 4.1%) but changes no outcome. The phase locking of fig1d was also measured with the phase from another shank than each unit's; the trough preference remains.
  • hpc units and channels are taken as CA1. CA3 recordings are left out of ripple analyses, as their CA1 reference channel is not in the files.
  • Where the paper does not state a test or model (Figure 1H, Figure 7E, the pair inclusion of Figure 4), the choice was fixed in the claims file before the analysis.

What was found about the dandiset:

  • No detected HFOs or ripples, no detection channels, and no unit waveforms, peak channels or quality metrics are deposited (the units table holds clu_id, group_id and location). Electrode coordinates are NaN in every file, and the probes are described only by their layout.
  • The LS and hippocampal channels share a 120-200 Hz signal: their phase difference is consistent even at random times, and many LS events fall on the same sample as CA1 ripples. Re-referencing within the LS shank reduces this. Some files list "reference sites a few millimeters dorsal" as a device; which reference each channel used is not stated.
  • Nine files have units without a region label (268 units); the hpc label does not separate CA1.
  • 25 units in 10 files have spike times out of order.
  • The CA3 recordings have no CA1 reference channel; the optogenetic rats are not in the dandiset.
  • Wide-band data, from which unit waveforms could be re-extracted, are in 27 of 98 files (DT1, DT2 and two DT9 files).
  • Spikes, LFP, sleep states and trials are consistent with one clock.
